Feedback and score for stories are channeled in <#1287942412211322904>, and not in <#1215710697162285108>.
Any Reporting Head may post the tip of the day in <#1508501517659930845>. You can even consult other Heads if you like, but it isn't generally needed.

Reporting Heads are free to schedule a post in any of the post scheduling channels. Our vision is to get posts out as soon as we can, and that can only be fulfilled if the schedule is posted on time. For news posts, it's imperative to schedule posts as soon as the word reaches a Reporting Head!

Discord begins archiving threads automatically after 7 days of inactivity. This is why the number of reporter threads visible might dwindle frequently. Bump those threads to keep them on everybody's channel list.

Feel free to ask reporters that haven't written a post in a long time to pick up a post. The Reporting Team has a lot of passive reporters at a given time, so it's effective to encourage less active reporters to pick up posts. Lesser active reporters could be encouraged to pick posts with later deadlines, while more active reporters can be asked to complete posts with sooner deadlines.

Reporting Heads want feedback for their posts too! If you believe you are not confident with what you have written, or would simply prefer another Reporting Head's input, you're free to do so! Just send the post details in <#1490863053200167045>, and another Editor should look at your work soon.

When editing, you also need to account for the accuracy of information. Editing isn't solely about checking formatting and language, but fact-checking against credible sources is an important task, too.

For reporters, the <#1539020197606719609> channel only appears on the channel list during the tournament season, to keep the channel list organized for reporters. When it isn't tournament season, the channel is suffixed with "-hidden" in its name. Reporting Heads enjoy full-time access to the channel!

The mission is to get posts out as soon as possible. Bear in mind that editing a post should not take more than 24 hours. Editing a post is generally easier than writing it, so give your fullest to editing!
Remember to remove Senior Reporters from threads they no longer need to assist in. Senior Reporters are welcome in other reporters' threads only when they need to assist the reporter in question!

Reporting Heads are expected to assist reporters when they ask for help. Please don't ghost reporters in their threads! You can also answer on behalf of another Reporting Head, especially if they are not responding. The goal is to make Reporting Team blazingly fast, so that posts are completed sooner.

When the stress on the Graphics Department is not high, request for a thumbnail through <#996166946049495191>. Posts with thumbnails gain greater attention from the army community. Visuals are key, and requesting a thumbnail for a post doesn't hurt!
A track record of reporters is kept in <#1532143843841933332>. Use this space to put up key information about certain reporters that may be useful to know in the future.
In the post feedback that you deliver to reporters, it's good to include what went well. It is a way of telling the reporter to "keep it up" with the well done parts of the post.
<#990197298891984996> is open to all reporters, and is useful for collaborative editing. You can also edit live for a reporter to see what you edit in realtime.

One-time thumbnails, such as those used in news posts, are posted in <#992802017271611482>. On the other hand, thumbnails that belong to a post series or those that are expected to be repeatedly used, are put up in <#988526331379740763>.

Just like reporter threads, there may be threads for posts, too! If you believe that a thread could be created for a long-term collaborative project, feel free to speak with other Reporting Heads on how they feel. <#1274754087723995146> is one example of a thread that belongs to a post, not a person.

Reporting Heads, you will love a challenge. [I challenge you to a Spot The Error game.](https://cpa-pengauthor.vercel.app/spot-the-error "Complete a Spot The Error challenge through the Pengauthor website.")

Please stick to editing just one post at a time! If you claim multiple posts to edit simultaneously, another Reporting Head who could have completed one of the edits sooner, would not be able to edit the post. In the Reporting Team, we really need to value efficiency and search for time-saving options, because we need to get posts out. Fast.
